where: Who would buy a $12 tiny bag of chips?
what_it_shows: Slow push-in on a real minibar price list, prices legible
job: The whole premise in one image — viewer reads the absurdity themselves before you say it

where: A $10 can of Coke. A $20 bottle of vodka the size of your thumb.
what_it_shows: Three fast cuts: chips, Coke, mini vodka, each held ~0.5s
job: Rhythm — matches the staccato of the line

where: WHO?
what_it_shows: Hard cut to black, white text: WHO?
job: The one-word-line-as-paragraph beat needs a visual equivalent, not just a pause

where: Sitting in a hotel room. Opening that little fridge.
what_it_shows: POV shot, hand opening minibar door in a dim room
job: Puts the viewer in the scene you're asking them to picture

where: really good night, or a really shitty one
what_it_shows: Two contrasting shots — celebration vs. someone face-down on a hotel bed
job: Lands the joke by literalizing both halves

where: I trained in hotel management
what_it_shows: Creator to camera, no b-roll
job: Deliberate absence — the credential lands harder unadorned

where: drink the mini vodka, refill the bottle with water
what_it_shows: Staged re-enactment: pour out, refill from tap, screw cap, place back, straighten it
job: The single best visual gag in the script. Worth shooting properly

where: 84% of them dealing with exactly this
what_it_shows: Animated stat card, 84% counting up
job: Makes a spoken number stick

where: a 10% buffer baked directly into every item
what_it_shows: Simple price-breakdown animation: $1 retail → stacked markup layers → $10
job: Shows a structure that's hard to hold in your head from audio alone

where: a stranger, in that same room, six months ago
what_it_shows: Empty hotel room, still, slightly eerie
job: Tonal shift — the joke gets briefly unsettling, which is the point

where: somebody has to physically open that fridge, count it, restock it
what_it_shows: Hotel staff restocking minibars / housekeeping cart footage
job: Shows invisible labor the viewer never considers

where: took eight full-time staff
what_it_shows: Eight figures appearing one by one
job: Absurdity is in the count — show the count

where: nobody starts their night at the minibar
what_it_shows: Busy hotel bar, early evening, full of people
job: Establishes the alternative the hotel already lost

where: that specific bacchanal desperation
what_it_shows: Same minibar as cue 1, now lit late-night, room messy
job: Visual rhyme with the opening — same object, different hour, whole thesis

where: one elevator ride away. Always.
what_it_shows: Elevator doors closing, floor numbers descending
job: Literalizes the thing you're being charged to avoid

where: not putting on pants
what_it_shows: On-screen text only, no footage
job: The button. Any literal image would over-explain it

where: shrinkage (English segment)
what_it_shows: Word on screen, definition beneath
job: Standard for the English-learning beat; keeps it skimmable

where: Siegas... Madison Hotel, Washington DC, 1963
what_it_shows: Exterior/interior of the Madison Hotel, 1960s; early minibar unit if it exists
job: Grounds the contested origin story in a real place

where: 1974, Hong Kong Hilton
what_it_shows: Hong Kong Hilton exterior, 1970s (demolished 1995, so archival is the only option)
job: Same — and the building no longer exists, which makes the footage inherently interesting

where: gets handed one of those 50ml whiskey bottles
what_it_shows: 1970s airline cabin service, or a mini bottle on a tray table
job: Recreates the founding anecdote

where: In-room drink sales jump 500%. Total hotel revenue up 5%
what_it_shows: Two bars climbing, 500% vs 5%
job: Two numbers in one sentence — audio alone loses one of them

where: weight sensors — actual load cells under every shelf
what_it_shows: Cutaway animation of a minibar shelf, load cell highlighted, item lifting, signal firing
job: Nobody knows what this looks like. This is the cue that most needs animation

where: infrared beams criss-crossing... like a heist movie
what_it_shows: Animated beam grid inside a minibar cabinet
job: Do NOT cut in actual heist-film footage — see licensing flags

where: charge you for picking something up and putting it back
what_it_shows: Hand lifts item, hesitates, replaces it — phone buzzes with a charge notification
job: The absurdity in one gesture

where: moved every bottle into a cabinet... got billed for all of it
what_it_shows: Itemized bill filling line by line, total climbing
job: Real story from the research, and bills-filling-up is inherently funny

where: pulled out all 1,946 minibars. In one building.
what_it_shows: Marriott Marquis Times Square exterior/atrium
job: Scale — the number needs a building attached to it

where: only 21% even wanted one
what_it_shows: 21% stat card
job: Consistent with cues 8/12

where: Louis XIII cognac... roughly €3,500
what_it_shows: Louis XIII decanter product shot
job: Brand imagery — see licensing flags

where: $400 luxury set, silk scarf included... $25 bottle of water with Swarovski crystals
what_it_shows: Fast cuts of each absurd item
job: Escalating montage — the pace is the joke

where: honesty bars — no sensors, no locks, nobody watching
what_it_shows: An unattended shelf of drinks, warm light, no barrier
job: Direct visual opposite of cue 22/23's surveillance tech — the contrast is the closing argument

where: Knowing you wouldn't put on pants.
what_it_shows: Return to the cue 1/14 minibar, now closed, room empty
job: Closes the visual loop the video opened on
